translationRepairs: He asked to treat him as a honored guest.
He asked to treat him as an honored guest.
上客 is 'honored guest'; English 'a honored' is an article error, and 'an honored' is the required grammatical fix.
Qin Hui's peace talk exiled loyal men and drained the realm's spirit.
When Qin Hui preached perverse talk to thwart them, loyal ministers and righteous men were cast out to die in the south, and the realm's spirit went slack.
Chinese 倡邪議以沮之 and 斥死南方 name perverse counsel thwarting resistance and loyal men cast out to die in the south; 'peace talk exiled' invents exile via peacemaking and drops those elements.
Whispers called you vain for glory; even the throne could not silence them, and you bore it seventeen years more.

Men then murmured against you in secret, saying you loved merit and ignored later trouble; even Your Majesty with exalted power could not prevail alone, and bore it in silence until now—another seventeen years.
Chinese 喜功名而不恤後患 and 不能以崇高之勢而獨勝之 are loving merit without regard for later trouble and inability to prevail alone; 'throne could not silence them' invents silencing.
At Bi, Luan Shu said, "Since Chu took Yong, its lord daily warned the people: 'Ah!
At the battle of Bi between Jin and Chu, Luan Shu said, "Since Chu took Yong, its lord daily warned the people: 'Ah!
晉、楚之戰於邲 names Jin and Chu fighting at Bi; bare 'At Bi' omits which states fought, and the repair restores that.
They eroded the state; even Zhang Dexiang and Chen Zhizhong could only slow the ruin.

Not only did they not aid the state's momentum, they further pared it away; though Zhang Dexiang and Chen Zhizhong in small part blocked them, how could the reformers not become discouraged themselves!
微章得象、陳執中以排沮 and 安得而不自沮哉 mark slight obstruction and the reformers' self-discouragement in a rhetorical question; 'slow the ruin' invents a different outcome.
They missed that the state thrived on divided power, light counties, and heavy center—slow but sure.

They did not know that the court's founding momentum suffered precisely from civil forms being too dense, powers too divided, commanderies too light below and too petty to rely on, and troops and wealth too concentrated above and too heavy and slow to mobilize.
正患文為之太密，事權之太分 names those conditions as the disease; 'thrived on divided power…slow but sure' reverses 正患 into a virtue.
When Song took the Mandate, the Qian house entered the capital and yielded the land.
When our Song received the Mandate, Chu brought his whole house to the capital and himself offered the soil.

Chapter 禘盡 is a corrupt personal-name reading; Wikisource has 俶盡, i.e. Qian Chu entirely bringing his house. Proposed 'Di Jin' invents a false name, while bare 'Qian house' still omits the personal subject.
Two centuries on it was Three Kingdoms ground; Zhuge Liang gathered Jing-Chu men and Shu lived;

Two hundred years more it became the three states' contested ground; Zhuge Liang from here rose to aid the First Lord; Jing-Chu scholars followed like clouds, and the Han house relied on this to survive again in Shu;
諸葛亮由此起輔先主 keeps 先主 as the one Zhuge Liang aided; the before text drops that referent.

Your Majesty resolutely moved the capital to Jianye; the hundred offices all followed from scratch; military and state ritual all followed simplicity; he also made a traveling palace at Wuchang to show intent not to dwell at ease.

Your Majesty resolutely moved the capital to Jianye; the hundred offices all followed from scratch; military and state ritual all followed simplicity; Your Majesty also made a traveling palace at Wuchang to show intent not to dwell at ease.
又作行宮 continues 陛下 as subject; 'he also made' wrongly shifts the agent away from Your Majesty.

Between xinmao and renchen he first withdrew to exhaust Heaven-and-Earth's creating beginning, examine past and present change, to push to the utmost the ways of emperor, king, hegemon, and lord, and obtain Han, Wei, Jin, and Tang's causes of length and shortness; the border of Heaven and man is bright and can be examined and known.

Between xinmao and renchen I first withdrew to exhaust Heaven-and-Earth's creating beginning, examine past and present change, to push to the utmost the ways of emperor, king, hegemon, and lord, and obtain Han, Wei, Jin, and Tang's causes of length and shortness; the border of Heaven and man is bright and can be examined and known.
Context 臣 and the memorial voice make the subject first person; 'he first withdrew' misattributes the speaker.
He first understood that today's Ruists who think they have the learning of rectifying heart and sincere intent are all men numb with wind paralysis who do not know pain or itch.
I first understood that today's Ruists who think they have the learning of rectifying heart and sincere intent are all men numb with wind paralysis who do not know pain or itch.
始悟 continues the memorialist's first-person realization; 'He first understood' misattributes it.
Your Majesty received him but did not charge him with affairs—your subject therefore admires Your Majesty's benevolence.
Your Majesty received me but did not charge me with affairs—your subject therefore admires Your Majesty's benevolence.
接之 points to the memorialist (臣); 'received him' invents a third-person object.
He further understood that today's talented ministers who think they have rich-state strong-army methods are all men mad and shouting wildly.
I further understood that today's talented ministers who think they have rich-state strong-army methods are all men mad and shouting wildly.
又悟 continues the same first-person memorial insight; 'He further understood' is the wrong person.

I foolishly think that the instruments by which the state has maintained itself are now exhausted, yet the great plan by which Emperor Yizu laid out the realm can still be relied upon for the long term. If we trace his intention back to its source and adapt it, recovery will not be difficult.

I foolishly think that the instruments by which the state has maintained itself are now exhausted, yet the great plan by which Emperor Taizu laid out the realm can still be relied upon for the long term. If we trace his intention back to its source and adapt it, recovery will not be difficult.
藝祖皇帝 is Song Taizu's conventional epithet; 'Emperor Yizu' invents a misleading English name against that usage.
Vice Minister He Dan had once been an examination official and demoted Liang; Liang was discontent and several times spoke insulting Dan; Dan heard and resented him, and at once forwarded the report.
Vice Minister He Dan had once been an examination official and failed Liang; Liang was discontent and several times spoke insulting Dan; Dan heard and resented him, and at once forwarded the report.
考試官，黜亮 in an examination setting means failing the candidate; 'demoted' invents removal from office.
Once officials heard of it, he had the boy beaten with the cudgel until the lad died and revived several times, but the servant still refused to admit guilt.
When the matter was reported to the authorities, the servant was flogged with the bamboo until he died and revived several times, yet still would not confess.
聞於官，笞榜僮 is a passive report that the servant was flogged; 'he had the boy beaten' invents an unauthorized agent.
Vice Minister Zheng Runan read the lone confession and exclaimed, 'Here is a wonder of the age.
Vice Minister Zheng Ruxie read the lone confession and exclaimed, 'Here is a wonder of the age.
鄭汝諧 romanizes as Zheng Ruxie (汝諧 Rúxié); Runan misreads 諧.
The vice minister Zheng Runan, reading the solitary testimony, was greatly astonished and said: 'This is a rare talent of the realm.
The vice minister Zheng Ruxie, reading the solitary testimony, was greatly astonished and said: 'This is a rare talent of the realm.
Same 鄭汝諧; literal Runan is the same wrong given-name reading, and Ruxie restores it.

When war was launched in the Kaixi era and the Jin watched the San Pass with urgency, Daochuan, on orders from the various offices to plan affairs, heard on the road that Wu Xi had rebelled; grief and rage showed in his face.

When war was launched in the Kaixi era and the Jin watched the San Pass with urgency, Daochuan, on orders from the various offices to plan affairs, then heard that Wu Xi had rebelled; grief and rage showed in his face.
道聞 after 道傳以諸司檄計事 continues Daochuan as subject (or 適聞 'then heard'); 'heard on the road' invents travel from 道.
Early in Jiading he became academy erudite, then court-of-sacrifices erudite and tutor in the Prince of Qi's school.
Early in Jiading he became academy erudite, then court-of-sacrifices erudite and tutor in the Prince of Yi's school.
沂王 is Prince of Yi (Yí); Qi would be 齊, so Prince of Qi is a wrong toponymic title.

At the beginning of the Jiading era he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then promoted to Erudite of the Court of Sacrifices while also instructing the primary school of the Prince of Qi's residence.

At the beginning of the Jiading era he was summoned as Erudite of the Imperial Academy, then promoted to Erudite of the Court of Sacrifices while also instructing the primary school of the Prince of Yi's residence.
Same 沂王; literal Prince of Qi repeats the 沂/齊 confusion, and Prince of Yi matches the graph.
As acting prefect of Xuan he enforced Zhu Xi's community granaries; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nanchang, and neighboring circuits followed suit and the people gained.
As acting prefect of Xuan he enforced Zhu Xi's community granaries; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nankang, and neighboring circuits followed suit and the people gained.
南康 is Nankang; Nanchang is 南昌, so the before text substitutes the wrong prefecture.
Acting as magistrate of Xuanzhou, he implemented Zhu Xi's community granary law; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nanchang, and other prefectures responded as one, and the people profited.
Acting as magistrate of Xuanzhou, he implemented Zhu Xi's community granary law; Shangrao, Xin'an, Nankang, and other prefectures responded as one, and the people profited.
Same 南康; literal Nanchang is the same wrong place-name, and Nankang restores it.
He had three sons—Dake, Dangke, and Xiankhe.
He had three sons—Dake, Dangke, and Xianke.
獻可 is Xianke; Xiankhe is a corrupted spelling of the same name.
Three sons: Dake, Dangke, and Xiankhe.
Three sons: Dake, Dangke, and Xianke.
Same 獻可; literal Xiankhe is the same corruption, and Xianke is the correct romanization.
